jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a preoperative verification process using a checklist or other mechanism to document verification of the following: • Informed consent that is appropriate to the procedure • Correct patient, correct procedure, and correct site • All required documents, blood products, medical equipment, and implantable medical devices are on hand, correct, and functional • Whether there is a risk of blood loss > 500 mL (7 mL/kg in children) • Whether the patient has a difficult airway or aspiration risk • Any known allergies (See also PCC.03.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.00, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Each patient’s surgical care is planned based on the results of the preoperative assessment and documented in the patient’s medical record.
jciRefs.meText: A preoperative diagnosis and the planned surgical procedure are documented in the patient’s medical record prior to the procedure.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ASC.04.00, ME 4

items.check: The site is marked with the hospital's single unambiguous mark, by the person doing the procedure, with the patient involved — and there are written alternatives for refusal, potential harm and technically impossible marking.
items.howToCheck: Observe a marking. Ask the patient if they were involved. Ask to see the three written alternatives.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the preoperative verification and surgical/invasive procedure site marking.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses an instantly recognizable and unambiguous mark for identifying the surgical/ invasive site that is consistent throughout the hospital.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the preoperative verification and surgical/invasive procedure site marking.
jciRefs.meText: The surgical/invasive site marking process includes the following: • Marking completed by the person performing the procedure • Patient involved in the marking process • Alternative site-marking process for cases in which marking may result in harm • Alternative site-identification process for patients who refuse site marking • Alternative site-marking techniques for situations in which routine site marking is not possible (for example, laser, stereotactic radiosurgery, dental)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.00, ME 3

items.check: The full team actively participates in a documented time-out in the procedure area immediately before starting, and a repeat time-out is performed before each new procedure by a different surgeon.
items.howToCheck: Observe a time-out. Watch whether everyone actually stops and participates.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the time-out that is performed immediately prior to the start of the surgical/invasive procedure and the sign-out that is conducted after the procedure.
jciRefs.meText: The full team actively participates in a time-out process, which includes the following elements in the area in which the surgical/invasive procedure will be performed, immediately before starting the procedure, and this is documented: • Correct patient identity • Correct procedure to be done • Correct surgical/invasive procedure site
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the time-out that is performed immediately prior to the start of the surgical/invasive procedure and the sign-out that is conducted after the procedure.
jciRefs.meText: When two or more separate procedures are being performed on the same patient by different surgeons, the team must perform another time-out before each new procedure is initiated.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.01, ME 4

items.check: A sign-out is conducted before the patient leaves the area, covering the procedure name, counts, specimen labelling and any equipment problems.
items.howToCheck: Observe the sign-out and listen for specimen labels being read aloud.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the time-out that is performed immediately prior to the start of the surgical/invasive procedure and the sign-out that is conducted after the procedure.
jciRefs.meText: Before the patient leaves the area in which the surgical/invasive procedure was performed, a sign-out process is conducted, which includes at least the following: • Name of the surgical/invasive procedure that was recorded/written • Completion of instrument, sponge, and needle counts, as applicable • Labeling of specimens • Any equipment problems to be addressed, as applicable
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.01, ME 2

items.check: Where radiation or imaging is used in this area, staff are trained, protective equipment is available and worn, and dose optimisation practice is followed.
items.howToCheck: Observe use. Check lead protection and the training record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: Radiology and diagnostic imaging staff are oriented to safety requirements and receive ongoing education and training for any new procedures, equipment, and hazardous materials. (See also SQE.01.07, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: Safety protective equipment and devices appropriate to the practices and hazards encountered from radiation and diagnostic imaging are available to staff, patients, and visitors, and in the area in which radiology and diagnostic imaging services are provided.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: Radiation safety education includes the principles of ALARA and implementation of protocols that identify the maximum dose of radiation for each type of study.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 4

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: Hazards from magnetic resonance imaging are addressed using industry standards and evidence-based guidelines.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 5

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital designates an individual to serve as the radiation safety officer who is responsible for the following: • Ensuring that radiologic services are provided in accordance with laws, regulation, and organizational policies • Monitoring compliance with established radiation safety practices (including oversight of dosimetry monitoring)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 6

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: The radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program is part of the organization’s facility management and infection prevention and control programs and provides reports to those programs at least annually and when any safety events and infection control events occur.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 7

items.check: Two approved patient identifiers are used before every intervention — and the room number or bed location is never one of them.
items.howToCheck: Observe a nurse from picking up the medication/specimen to the bedside. Ask which two identifiers this hospital approves.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe: Staff Nurse. Ask: Staff Nurse, Charge Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process to improve accuracy of patient identifications.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses at least two patient identifiers, that do not include the use of the patient’s room number or location in the hospital, to identify the patient and to label elements associated with the patient’s care and treatment plan. (See also MMU.04.01, ME 4; MMU.05.03, ME 4; MOI.03.00, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.01.00, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process to improve accuracy of patient identifications.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital identifies patients with at least two identifiers before performing diagnostic procedures, providing treatments, and performing other procedures. (See also MMU.04.01, ME 4)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.01.00, ME 2

items.check: Specimens are labelled at the bedside at the moment of collection, and transport/storage follows the written procedure.
items.howToCheck: Observe a collection if possible. Otherwise trace one specimen from the unit to the laboratory.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Procedures for collecting, identifying, handling, safely transporting, and disposing of specimens are established and implemented.
jciRefs.meText: Procedures are established and implemented for the collection and identification of specimens.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.03.06, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: Procedures for collecting, identifying, handling, safely transporting, and disposing of specimens are established and implemented.
jciRefs.meText: Procedures are established and implemented for the transport, storage, and preservation of specimens.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.03.06, ME 3

items.check: Outpatients at fall risk because of their condition, diagnosis, situation or location are screened, and where risk is identified the fall-reduction interventions are in place and documented. (Not a blanket screen of every outpatient.)
items.howToCheck: Ask which outpatient situations trigger fall screening here, check one such record, then look for the interventions physically present.
items.evidenceAskWho: Ask: Charge Nurse. Review Medical Record. Observe.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital develops and implements a process to reduce the risk of falls, and patient harm resulting from falls.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital screens all outpatients whose condition, diagnosis, situation, or location may put them at risk for falls and uses screening tools appropriate for the patients being served.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.02.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital develops and implements a process to reduce the risk of falls, and patient harm resulting from falls.
jciRefs.meText: Interventions to reduce fall risk are implemented for those identified patients, situations, and locations within the hospital assessed to be at risk, and the interventions are documented.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.02.00, ME 4

items.check: All seven pre-administration checks are performed — identity, order-to-label match, visual inspection, expiry, contraindications, correct time/dose/route, escalation of any unresolved concern — and every dose given is recorded at a time consistent with the order.
items.howToCheck: Observe one full medication administration from preparation to the bedside, then compare the MAR against the order for that patient.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe: Staff Nurse. Review Medical Record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medication administration is safely performed by qualified individuals.
jciRefs.meText: Prior to administration, the individual administering the medication must do the following: • Verify the identity of the patient. • Verify that the medication selected matches the medication order or prescription and product label, including time, frequency, dose, and route. • Visually inspect the medication for particulates, discoloration, or other loss of integrity. • Verify that the medication has not expired. • Verify that no known contraindications exist. • Verify that the medication is being administered at the proper time, in the prescribed dose, and by the correct route. • Discuss unresolved concerns about the medication with the patient’s physician or health care practitioner (if different from the physician or health care practitioner) and/or staff involved with the patient’s care, treatment, and services according to hospital policy.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.06.00, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medication administration is safely performed by qualified individuals.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a process for medication administration to verify that the medication is correctly administered in accordance with the medication prescription or order. (See also MMU.05.02, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.06.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medication administration is safely performed by qualified individuals.
jciRefs.meText: Medications are administered as prescribed on a timely basis, and each dose is recorded in the patient’s medical record.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.06.00, ME 4

items.check: Medications are prepared in a clean, uncluttered, functionally separate area; staff visually inspect the product; and single-use / multi-dose vial rules are followed — vials dated on opening, no re-entry with a used needle.
items.howToCheck: Observe the preparation area and one preparation. Then inspect every vial currently open on the unit and ask the nurse to state the rule.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are prepared and dispensed in a safe and clean environment.
jciRefs.meText: Medications are prepared and dispensed in clean, uncluttered, safe, and functionally separate areas with appropriate medical equipment and supplies. (See also PCI.04.00, MEs 1 and 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.05.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are prepared and dispensed in a safe and clean environment.
jciRefs.meText: During preparation, staff visually inspect the medication for particulates, discoloration, or other loss of integrity.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.05.00, ME 4

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are prepared and dispensed in a safe and clean environment.
jciRefs.meText: Guidelines for use of single-use and multidose vials are identified and implemented in the medication processes.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.05.00, ME 5

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are properly and safely stored.
jciRefs.meText: Medications and chemicals used to prepare medications are accurately labeled with contents, expiration dates, and applicable warnings.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.00, ME 4

items.check: Medication storage walk: correct storage conditions with monitored temperature and a documented response to excursions; all medications including controlled substances secured against diversion and accurately accounted for; no expired stock in active supply and expired items segregated and labelled 'Expired'.
items.howToCheck: Walk every medication storage point on the unit — room, fridge, carts, procedure trolleys. Check the temperature log, the controlled drug count, and every expiry date you can reach.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Review temperature and count records. Ask: Charge Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are properly and safely stored.
jciRefs.meText: Medications are stored under conditions suitable for product stability, including medications stored on individual patient care units and ambulances, as applicable. (See also IPSG.03.02, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.00, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are properly and safely stored.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital stores all medications, including biologicals and controlled (scheduled) medications, in a secured area to prevent diversion, and locked, as applicable, in accordance with laws and regulations. These medications are accurately accounted for according to applicable laws and regulations. (See also IPSG.03.02, ME 2; FMS.05.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are properly and safely stored.
jciRefs.meText: Medications are protected from loss or theft throughout the hospital. (See also FMS.04.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.00, ME 6

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a process for handling expired medications.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital isolates expired medications from the rest of the medication stock to prevent accidental use or distribution and clearly labels them as “Expired.”
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.01.03, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a process for handling expired medications.
jciRefs.meText: The process includes documentation of all actions taken related to the expired medication.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.01.03, ME 3

items.check: High-alert medications carry the hospital's standard safeguards everywhere, plus any additional safeguard the hospital has defined for a specific drug.
items.howToCheck: Ask to see the high-alert list, then check the safeguards physically applied to one such medication in use here.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Ask: Staff Nurse, Charge Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process to improve the safety of high-alert medications.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a risk mitigation strategy for reducing the risk of harm from high-alert medications that is uniform throughout the hospital and, in addition, includes tailored strategies for specific medications when necessary.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.03.00, ME 2

items.check: Look-alike / sound-alike medications are separated in storage and differentiated so they cannot be confused.
items.howToCheck: Ask to see the LASA list, then find two LASA medications stocked here and check how they are separated.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process to improve the safety of look-alike/sound-alike medications.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a process for managing look-alike/sound-alike medications that is comprehensive and uniform throughout the hospital. (See also MMU.07.01, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.03.01, ME 2

items.check: Concentrated electrolytes are segregated, labelled with warnings, and accessible only to qualified trained staff — and are held here only if hospital policy approves this location.
items.howToCheck: Ask which locations policy approves. Then search this unit's storage to confirm nothing is held outside that approval.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process to manage the safe use of concentrated electrolytes.
jciRefs.meText: Only qualified and trained individuals have access to concentrated electrolytes, and they are labeled with appropriate warnings and segregated from other medications throughout the storage and dispensing process. (See also MMU.04.00, ME 1; MMU.04.01, MEs 4 and 5; MMU.05.00, ME 1; MMU.05.03, ME 4)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.03.02, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process to manage the safe use of concentrated electrolytes.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital only stores vials of concentrated electrolytes outside of the pharmacy for emergency situations or specific purposes, and these are clearly identified in hospital policy. (See also MMU.03.00, MEs 1 and 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.03.02, ME 2

items.check: Emergency medications are immediately available, and the emergency cart opens without needing a specific person or a key.
items.howToCheck: Ask the nurse to open the emergency cart in front of you without calling anyone.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Emergency medications are available, uniformly stored, monitored, and secure when stored out of the pharmacy.
jciRefs.meText: Emergency medications are immediately available in the patient care areas or are readily accessible within the hospital to meet emergency needs.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Emergency medications are available, uniformly stored, monitored, and secure when stored out of the pharmacy.
jciRefs.meText: Access to emergency medications shall not require a specific individual or keys to unlock the emergency cart.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.01, ME 3

items.check: Current drug information is available at the point of care at any hour.
items.howToCheck: Ask the nurse to show you what they use at 2 a.m. when unsure about a medication.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital manages its medication management processes.
jciRefs.meText: Appropriate and updated sources of drug information are readily available to those involved in medication use.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.01.00, ME 7

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medication prescriptions or orders are reviewed for appropriateness.
jciRefs.meText: Clinical decision support programs used in conjunction with a designated licensed professional or trained individual for the full appropriateness review, as well as other computer programs and print reference materials used to cross-check the critical elements of an appropriateness review, are current and updated.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.05.02, ME 6

items.check: If a medication were recalled today, staff know how they would find out, where it would be held, and that it must be labelled 'Recalled'.
items.howToCheck: Ask the Charge Nurse to describe the process and show the holding location.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a medication recall system process.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital isolates recalled medications from the rest of the medication stock to prevent accidental use or distribution and clearly labels them as “Recalled.”
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.01.02, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a medication recall system process.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital has a process to inform health care providers about the recall and advise them on alternative treatments if necessary.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.01.02, ME 5

items.check: Self-administration or patient-own medication is only permitted where policy allows, competency is determined first, and the five required education elements are documented.
items.howToCheck: Find a self-administering patient and check the competency determination and the education record.
items.evidenceAskWho: Review Medical Record. Ask patient to demonstrate.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Policies and procedures govern medications brought into the hospital by the patient or family, medication prescribed for patient self-administration, and medication samples.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital educates patients and families involved in self-administration and documents in the patient’s medical record about the following: • Medication name, type, and reason for use • How to administer the medication, including process, time, frequency, route, and dose • Anticipated actions and potential side effects of the medication administered • Monitoring the effects of the medication • Proper storage of the medication
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.06.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: Policies and procedures govern medications brought into the hospital by the patient or family, medication prescribed for patient self-administration, and medication samples.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital determines that the patient or the family member who administers the medication is competent at medication administration before allowing them to administer medications.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.06.01, ME 4

items.check: Special-handling medications (hazardous, radioactive, investigational) used here follow the written special-handling process.
items.howToCheck: Ask which apply on this unit and observe the handling and PPE in use.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Medications are properly and safely stored.
jciRefs.meText: There is a written process for managing medications or products requiring special handling, such as hazardous medications, radioactive medications, and investigational medications. (See also MMU.06.00, ME 6)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MMU.03.00, ME 3

items.check: Hand hygiene is performed at the moments the adopted guideline defines and staff can name them; liquid soap, running water, hand disinfectant and single-use towels are available where required; and there are no hand air dryers in patient care areas.
items.howToCheck: Observe at least five hand hygiene opportunities. Then walk every sink and dispenser on the unit and ask one nurse to list the moments.
items.mes: IPSG.05.00 ME 2; PCI.07.01 ME 5; PCI.07.01 ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements evidence-based hand-hygiene guidelines to reduce the risk of health care–associated infections.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements an evidence-based hand hygiene program throughout the hospital. (See also PCI.07.01, MEs 2, 5, and 6)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.05.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides resources and equipment to protect staff, health care practitioners, patients, and visitors from biological, physical, and chemical hazards, and these are readily available for use.
jciRefs.meText: Liquid soap and running water, hand disinfectants, and single-use towels are provided in areas where handwashing and hand-disinfecting procedures are required, and hand air dryers are not used in patient care areas. (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.01, ME 5

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides resources and equipment to protect staff, health care practitioners, patients, and visitors from biological, physical, and chemical hazards, and these are readily available for use.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital ensures that appropriate personal protective equipment and hand hygiene agents are readily available when needed. (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2; FMS.09.01, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.01, ME 2

items.check: Correct PPE is stocked at the point of care and staff don and doff it in the correct sequence.
items.howToCheck: Ask a nurse to don and doff the PPE for a patient here and talk through the sequence.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides resources and equipment to protect staff, health care practitioners, patients, and visitors from biological, physical, and chemical hazards, and these are readily available for use.
jciRefs.meText: Staff are trained and correctly use personal protective equipment in each identified situation.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides resources and equipment to protect staff, health care practitioners, patients, and visitors from biological, physical, and chemical hazards, and these are readily available for use.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital ensures that appropriate personal protective equipment and hand hygiene agents are readily available when needed. (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2; FMS.09.01, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.01, ME 2

items.check: Isolation precautions match the organism — signage, PPE, placement and transport arrangements are all consistent, and precautions start on suspicion, not only on confirmation.
items.howToCheck: Take an isolation patient and check every element from the door signage inward.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Review Medical Record. Ask: Staff Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital protects patients, visitors, and staff from transmission of infections and communicable diseases.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses a process to isolate patients with infectious diseases, and staff use transmission- based precautions, in accordance with recommended guidelines. (See also FMS.09.01, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.00, ME 1

items.check: Shared and non-critical equipment is cleaned with the approved product, at the correct dilution, for the full contact time stated on the label.
items.howToCheck: Ask a nurse to clean a shared device and state the contact time for the wipe being used.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with medical/surgical equipment, devices, and supplies by proper cleaning, disinfection, sterilization, and storage.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements proper infection prevention and control practices when cleaning and performing low-level and intermediate-level disinfection of noncritical medical equipment, devices, and supplies that address the following: • Use of approved disinfectants in accordance with the product label directions, including the indication, specified-use dilution when applicable, contact time, and method of application • Use of disinfectant agents and methods approved by the equipment or device manufacturers
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.03.00, ME 1

items.check: Clean and sterile supplies are stored so contamination and damage are prevented, under the manufacturer's conditions, with no expired or damaged stock in usable supply.
items.howToCheck: Inspect the whole store room and at least one procedure trolley.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with medical/surgical equipment, devices, and supplies by proper cleaning, disinfection, sterilization, and storage.
jciRefs.meText: Cleaned, disinfected, and sterilized equipment, devices, and supplies are properly stored in designated storage areas that prevent contamination prior to use.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.03.00, ME 6

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for managing expired and damaged devices and supplies.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a process to manage expired supplies.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.03.02, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for managing expired and damaged devices and supplies.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a process to manage damaged supplies.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.03.02, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for managing expired and damaged devices and supplies.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital stores supplies in a manner that prevents contamination or damage, and under environmental conditions recommended by the manufacturer when applicable.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.03.02, ME 3

items.check: Sharps containers are dedicated, closable, puncture-proof, leakproof and never reused; sharps are handled safely from the moment of withdrawal; and infectious waste, blood and body fluids are segregated correctly from bedside to the point waste leaves the unit.
items.howToCheck: Check every sharps container. Observe one sharp being handled. Then follow the waste route.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements processes for proper disposal of waste, proper management of human tissues, and safe handling and disposal of sharps and needles.
jciRefs.meText: Sharps and needles are collected in dedicated, closable, puncture-proof, leakproof containers that are not reused.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.05.00, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements processes for proper disposal of waste, proper management of human tissues, and safe handling and disposal of sharps and needles.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital identifies and implements practices to reduce the risk of injury and infection from the handling and management of sharps and needles.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.05.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements processes for proper disposal of waste, proper management of human tissues, and safe handling and disposal of sharps and needles.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements practices to reduce the risk of infection from handling and disposal of infectious waste, blood and blood components, body fluids, and body tissues. (See also FMS.05.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.05.00, ME 1

items.check: Staff know exactly what to do after a needlestick at any hour — for staff, and also for a patient or visitor exposure.
items.howToCheck: Ask a night-shift nurse to walk through it end to end.
items.evidenceAskWho: Ask: Staff Nurse. Review education record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with exposure to blood, body fluids, and other potentially infectious materials.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses an expeditious process for reporting patient, staff, and visitor exposures to blood and body fluids that is timely.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.05.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with exposure to blood, body fluids, and other potentially infectious materials.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses a process for acting on patient, staff, and visitor exposures to blood and body fluids.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.05.01, ME 4

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with exposure to blood, body fluids, and other potentially infectious materials.
jciRefs.meText: Staff are educated in the process for reporting an exposure incident.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.05.01, ME 5

items.check: Clean and soiled linen never cross, and linen from an isolation room is handled with the correct precautions.
items.howToCheck: Trace the linen route on this unit in both directions.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The infection prevention and control program follows evidence-based guidelines related to cleaning and disinfection of laundry, linens, and scrub attire provided by the hospital.
jciRefs.meText: Laundry, linens, and hospital-issued scrub attire are transported, processed, and stored in a manner that prevents cross contamination of soiled and clean items.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.04.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The infection prevention and control program follows evidence-based guidelines related to cleaning and disinfection of laundry, linens, and scrub attire provided by the hospital.
jciRefs.meText: Standard precautions are used when handling laundry, linens, and hospital-issued scrub attire, and appropriate transmission-based precautions are used as indicated by infection risk.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.04.01, ME 2

items.check: Staff know who to contact with an infection control question at night, can describe recent IPC support to this unit, and can state this unit's current infection results.
items.howToCheck: Ask two nurses, including one on night shift if possible. Look for how unit IPC results are displayed or communicated.
items.evidenceAskWho: Ask: Staff Nurse, Charge Nurse. Observe.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital coordinates infection prevention and control activities across all departments and services.
jciRefs.meText: The infection prevention and control program supports staff throughout the hospital for infection prevention and control activities.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.01.01, ME 5

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides education on infection prevention and control practices to staff, health care practitioners, patients, families, and others when indicated by their role in the hospital.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital communicates findings and trends from the infection prevention and control program activities to all staff.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.08.01, ME 4

items.check: The special pathogen protocol is physically available at the point of care and staff can apply the entry screening step.
items.howToCheck: Ask to see it at the nurses' station and ask the nurse to describe screening at the door.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements processes to support preparedness for epidemiologically significant infectious diseases or special pathogens.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements protocols for high-consequence infectious diseases or special pathogens, that are readily available for use at the point of care and address the following: • Procedures for screening at the points of entry to the hospital for respiratory symptoms, fever, rash, and travel history to identify or initiate evaluation for high-consequence diseases or special pathogens. (See also FMS.09.01, ME 3) Note: Points of entry may include the emergency department, urgent care, and ambulatory clinics. • Patient isolation procedures • Procedures for informing public health authorities and key hospital staff • Procedures for required personal protective equipment and proper donning and doffing techniques • Infection control procedures to support continued and safe provision of care while the patient is in isolation and to reduce exposure among staff, patients, and visitors • Procedures for waste management and cleaning and disinfecting patient care spaces, surfaces, and equipment
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.02, ME 1

items.check: Privacy and dignity are protected during interviews, examinations, procedures and transport off the unit.
items.howToCheck: Observe a clinical interaction. Ask a patient whether they felt their dignity was maintained during personal care.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital protects patient privacy, confidentiality, and access to health information.
jciRefs.meText: Patient privacy is respected for all clinical interviews, examinations, procedures/treatments, and transport. (See also GLD.09.00, ME 3; HCT.01.03, ME 2; MOI.01.01, ME 1; MOI.01.02, ME 3)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.01.02, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital respects, protects, and promotes patient rights.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital treats the patient in a respectful manner that supports the patient’s dignity.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.01.01, ME 3

items.check: Patients receive information about their rights in a language they understand, and know how to raise a complaint — with the information visible on the unit.
items.howToCheck: Ask a patient what they were told about their rights and how they would raise a concern. Then look for both displayed on the unit.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital respects, protects, and promotes patient rights.
jciRefs.meText: Information about patient rights and responsibilities is provided to each patient in a language the patient understands. (See also MOI.02.02, ME 3)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.01.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital informs patients and families about their right to report complaints and to be notified of errors related to their care and the hospital’s process for acting on them.
jciRefs.meText: Patients and families are informed about the process for reporting complaints. (See also APR.09.00, MEs 1 and 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.02.03, ME 1

items.check: Vulnerable patients identified on this unit have the specific protections the hospital's policy defines actually in place.
items.howToCheck: Take one vulnerable patient and show what is different about their care right now.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Review Medical Record. Ask: Staff Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital identifies its vulnerable populations and the risks to those populations.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital establishes a written policy and implements a process to identify how risks are managed for each vulnerable population. (See also PCI.07.00, ME 2; HRP.02.02, ME 3)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.01.04, ME 4

items.check: Patients are told when there is a delay in care, the reason, and the alternatives — and unusual delays are documented.
items.howToCheck: Ask a waiting patient. Then look for the delay entry in a record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital considers the clinical needs of patients and informs patients when there are unusual delays for diagnostic and/or treatment services.
jciRefs.meText: Patients are informed when there will be a delay in care and/or treatment.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.02, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital considers the clinical needs of patients and informs patients when there are unusual delays for diagnostic and/or treatment services.
jciRefs.meText: Patients are informed of the reasons for the delay and provided with information on available alternatives consistent with their clinical needs.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.02, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital considers the clinical needs of patients and informs patients when there are unusual delays for diagnostic and/or treatment services.
jciRefs.meText: The information on unusual delays and reasons for the delay are documented in the patient’s medical record.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.02, ME 3

items.check: Understanding is verified — the patient can demonstrate or restate. A signature or attendance is not enough.
items.howToCheck: Ask the patient to show you how they will do what they were taught.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Ask patient. Ask: Staff Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Each patient’s educational needs and learning ability are assessed and documented in their medical record.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital has a process to verify that patients and families acknowledge receipt and understanding of the education provided. (See also ACC.04.01, ME 5) Section III: Health Care Organization Management Standards
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.04.01, ME 3

items.check: Patients and visitors are taught hand hygiene, when isolation precautions apply, and how to use PPE correctly.
items.howToCheck: Ask a visitor outside an isolation room what they were told before entering.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides resources and equipment to protect staff, health care practitioners, patients, and visitors from biological, physical, and chemical hazards, and these are readily available for use.
jciRefs.meText: Patients and visitors are educated on when they are required to disinfect their hands, when transmission based precautions such as isolation precaution must be followed, and how to correctly use personal protective equipment when applicable. (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.07.01, ME 6

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides education on infection prevention and control practices to staff, health care practitioners, patients, families, and others when indicated by their role in the hospital.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital provides education about infection prevention and control to patients and families.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCI.08.01, ME 3

items.check: Handover follows the hospital's standardised process for this handover type, critical information transfers, and the receiving nurse has a real opportunity to ask questions — handover is two-way, not a read-out.
items.howToCheck: Observe a full shift handover and watch specifically for the clarification moment. If none occurs, ask the receiving nurse when they can query.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a standardized process for handover communication.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a standardized procedure to communicate critical information between health care practitioners during handovers of patient care.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.02.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a standardized process for handover communication.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses standardized forms, tools, or methods that support a consistent and complete handover process that includes the opportunity for all staff involved to clarify information and ask questions.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.02.01, ME 2

items.check: Staff can access all the information they need for safe care of this patient right now.
items.howToCheck: Stand at a workstation and ask the nurse to retrieve everything they need for one patient.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital retrieves, disseminates, and transmits health information on a timely basis in a format that meets user expectations, and with the desired frequency.
jciRefs.meText: Staff providing patient care have access to the data and information needed to carry out their job responsibilities and provide patient care safely and effectively.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.02.03, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital provides continuous patient care services and coordination among health care providers.
jciRefs.meText: The patient’s medical record is available to those practitioners who are authorized to have access and need it for the care of the patient. (See also MOI.01.01, ME 4)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.03.00, ME 2

items.check: There is a systematic process to recognise deterioration, with documented age-specific early warning criteria in use here.
items.howToCheck: Ask the nurse what criteria they use and find them documented on the unit.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Ask: Staff Nurse. Review Medical Record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Clinical staff are trained to recognize and respond to changes in a patient’s condition.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital has a systematic process to recognize and respond to changes or deterioration of patient condition.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — COP.03.00, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Clinical staff are trained to recognize and respond to changes in a patient’s condition.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements documented age-specific early warning criteria describing early signs of a change or deterioration in a patient’s condition.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — COP.03.00, ME 2

items.check: Resuscitation equipment and medications appropriate to the population here are available, and ALS arrives within the time the standard requires.
items.howToCheck: Check the trolley contents against the population served. Ask what the response time is at night.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Resuscitation services are available throughout the hospital.
jciRefs.meText: Medical equipment for resuscitation and medications for basic and advanced life support are standardized and available for use based on the populations served. (See also MMU.03.01, ME 4)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — COP.04.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: Resuscitation services are available throughout the hospital.
jciRefs.meText: In all areas of the hospital, basic life support is initiated immediately upon recognition of cardiac or respiratory arrest, and advanced life support is initiated in fewer than 5 minutes.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — COP.04.00, ME 3

items.check: Equipment in use on patients here is inventoried and carries current inspection, testing or calibration evidence.
items.howToCheck: Check the labels on three devices currently connected to patients.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital develops and implements a program for the management of medical equipment throughout the organization.
jciRefs.meText: The equipment program includes the following: • An inventory of all medical equipment • Regular inspections when equipment is new and as required by manufacturers’ guidelines • Testing according to use and manufacturers’ requirements • Documentation of results • Performance of preventive maintenance and calibration as applicable • Adherence to local laws and regulations (See also AOP.03.04, ME 2; AOP.05.04, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.07.00, ME 2

items.check: Staff involved in laser or electrosurgical use are trained, the required PPE is worn, and controls are in place.
items.howToCheck: Observe a case using the device. Check eye protection and the training record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital establishes and implements a program for the safe use of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices used for performing procedures and treatments.
jciRefs.meText: All staff involved in the use of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices receive safety training and continuing education; the training and ongoing education are documented.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — HCT.02.00, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital establishes and implements a program for the safe use of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices used for performing procedures and treatments.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital establishes and implements administrative and engineering controls for the laser, electrosurgical, and optical radiation safety program to promote safety and prevent injury for patients and staff.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — HCT.02.00, ME 4

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital establishes and implements a program for the safe use of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices used for performing procedures and treatments.
jciRefs.meText: Personal protective equipment appropriate to the type of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices and type of procedures is available for staff and patients, and staff use it correctly and ensure that patients and staff are protected during procedures.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — HCT.02.00, ME 5

items.check: Only authorised individuals access records and make entries, each within their approved level — no shared logins.
items.howToCheck: Watch how staff log in. Ask the nurse what they can and cannot access.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements processes to ensure that data and information are accessed by authorized individuals only and in accordance with their level of access. (See also ACC.03.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.01.01, ME 4

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements processes to ensure that only authorized individuals make entries in the patient medical record and in accordance with their level of access.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.01.01, ME 5

items.check: EMR screens are not left unattended displaying patient information, workstations are secured per hospital policy, and patient information is not visible to unauthorised persons — whiteboards, screens facing corridors, notes at the bedside.
items.howToCheck: Walk the nurses' station, corridors and treatment rooms unannounced. Then stand where a visitor would stand and note what you can read. Check against the hospital's own policy — do not apply a screen-lock time limit of your own.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements processes consistent with laws and regulations to ensure the confidentiality, security, and integrity of data and information. (See also PCC.01.02, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.01.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital protects patient privacy, confidentiality, and access to health information.
jciRefs.meText: Confidentiality of patient information is maintained according to laws and regulations.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.01.02, ME 2

items.check: Paper records, printed handover sheets, labels and reports are not left exposed; confidential material is disposed of securely; and passwords or credentials are not shared or written down where others can see them.
items.howToCheck: Check the nurses' station, trolleys, printer trays, handover boards, monitors, drawers and the shredding point. Ask the nurse what they do when a colleague asks to use their login.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital protects patient privacy, confidentiality, and access to health information.
jciRefs.meText: Confidentiality of patient information is maintained according to laws and regulations.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — PCC.01.02, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements processes consistent with laws and regulations to ensure the confidentiality, security, and integrity of data and information. (See also PCC.01.02, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.01.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements processes to ensure that data and information are accessed by authorized individuals only and in accordance with their level of access. (See also ACC.03.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.01.01, ME 4

items.check: Staff know what to do when the EMR goes down — where the downtime forms are and how care continues.
items.howToCheck: Ask a nurse to produce the downtime pack and describe the first four hours.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital develops, maintains, and tests a program for response to planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
jciRefs.meText: Staff are trained in the strategies and tactics used for planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — HCT.01.04, ME 6

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital develops, maintains, and tests a program for response to planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
jciRefs.meText: The program includes continuity strategies for the provision of ongoing safe, high-quality patient care and services, including services provided by outside vendors, during planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — HCT.01.04, ME 3

items.check: Staff know how to access the policies relevant to their work, and practice on the unit matches them.
items.howToCheck: Ask a nurse to find one policy relevant to a task they do daily.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Leaders review, approve, and manage implementation of policies and procedures that guide and support patient care and services.
jciRefs.meText: Required policies, procedures, and plans are available, and staff understand how to access those documents relevant to their responsibilities.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.02.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Leaders review, approve, and manage implementation of policies and procedures that guide and support patient care and services.
jciRefs.meText: The requirements of the policies, procedures, and plans are fully implemented and evident in the actions of individual staff members.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — MOI.02.01, ME 3

items.check: Restricted and security-risk areas on this unit are identified and access is controlled.
items.howToCheck: Walk the unit and try the doors that should be secured.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a program to provide a secure environment for patients, families, staff, and visitors.
jciRefs.meText: The security program identifies all security risk areas and restricted areas and ensures that they are monitored and kept secure. (See also COP.05.00, ME 1; MMU.03.00, ME 6; MMU.03.01, ME 2; PCC.01.03, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.04.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a program to provide a secure environment for patients, families, staff, and visitors.
jciRefs.meText: The security program ensures that relevant patients, as well as staff, students, trainees, contract workers, volunteers, vendors, and individuals associated with independent business entities, are identified.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.04.00, ME 3

items.check: Staff can describe and demonstrate the fire response and how they would bring patients to safety from here; exit routes are free and unobstructed with visible signage and working emergency lighting.
items.howToCheck: Ask a nurse to walk you through the response physically, following the exit route with you.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital conducts regular exercises with staff to evaluate the fire safety program.
jciRefs.meText: Staff who provide patient care can describe and demonstrate how to bring patients to safety.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.06.03, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital conducts regular exercises with staff to evaluate the fire safety program.
jciRefs.meText: All hospital personnel, including the night shift and weekends, are trained in the fire safety program and participate in drills to evaluate the fire safety program at least annually, or more frequently when required by laws and regulations or other authorities.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.06.03, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains fire safety equipment and fire safety building features.
jciRefs.meText: The fire safety program includes the safe exit from the facility through free and unobstructed access to exits.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.06.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains fire safety equipment and fire safety building features.
jciRefs.meText: The fire safety program includes clearly visible exit signage that is understandable to the hospital’s occupants.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.06.01, ME 4

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital maintains fire safety equipment and fire safety building features.
jciRefs.meText: The fire safety program includes lighting for emergency exit corridors and stairs.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.06.01, ME 5

items.check: Staff can describe the handling and spill precautions for the hazardous materials used here, and the safety information is accessible at the point of use.
items.howToCheck: Ask what would happen for a spill of the specific agent used on this unit, and ask to see the safety information.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a program for the management of hazardous materials and waste.
jciRefs.meText: Staff can describe and/or demonstrate precautions and procedures for handling and managing hazardous materials and waste, as applicable to the staff member’s role and responsibilities.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.05.00, ME 7

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a program for the management of hazardous materials and waste.
jciRefs.meText: Information about the hazardous materials related to safe handling, spill-handling procedures, and procedures for managing exposures are up to date and available at all times.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.05.00, ME 6

items.check: Staff know what to do when power, water or medical gas fails on this unit.
items.howToCheck: Ask the nurse. Check that utility controls serving this area are labelled.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital utility systems program ensures that essential utilities, including power, water, and medical gases, are available at all times, and alternative sources for essential utilities are tested and evaluated.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital ensures backup availability/continuity of essential utilities (including power, water, and medical gas) 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. (See also FMS.09.00, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.08.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a program for the management of utility systems throughout the organization.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital labels utility system controls to facilitate partial or complete emergency shutdowns.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.08.00, ME 5

items.check: Where construction or maintenance work adjoins this unit, the risk assessment was completed and the controls are physically in place.
items.howToCheck: Inspect the barrier and controls. Ask for the assessment.

jciRefs.standardStatement: When planning for construction, renovation, and demolition projects, or maintenance activities that affect patient care, the organization conducts a preconstruction risk assessment.
jciRefs.meText: When planning for construction, renovation, or demolition projects, or maintenance activities that affect patient care, the hospital conducts a preconstruction risk assessment (PCRA) that includes, at minimum, the following: • Air quality • Infection prevention and control • Utilities • Noise • Vibration • Hazardous materials and waste • Fire safety • Security • Emergency procedures, including alternate pathways/exits and access to emergency services • Other hazards that affect care, treatment, and services (See also FMS.02.00, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.10.00, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: When planning for construction, renovation, and demolition projects, or maintenance activities that affect patient care, the organization conducts a preconstruction risk assessment.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital takes action based on its assessment to minimize risks during construction, renovation, and demolition projects, and maintenance activities that affect patient care.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — FMS.10.00, ME 2

items.check: Today's assignment was built against each nurse's licence, training and experience, and a nurse performing a high-risk task here has documented competency specific to THAT task — not a general competency form.
items.howToCheck: Take today's assignment sheet and ask the Charge Nurse to justify two assignments. Then pick a high-risk task happening now and ask for the matching competency evidence.
items.evidenceAskWho: Review assignment and competency records. Observe. Ask: Charge Nurse, Head Nurse.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a standardized process to identify job responsibilities and to plan clinical work assignments based on the nursing staff member’s credentials and any regulatory requirements.
jciRefs.meText: Licensure, education, training, and experience of a nursing staff member are used to plan clinical work assignments.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — SQE.03.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a standardized process to identify job responsibilities and to plan clinical work assignments based on the nursing staff member’s credentials and any regulatory requirements.
jciRefs.meText: Core criteria for evaluating nursing staff in the program include, at a minimum, current licensure, and current competence.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — SQE.03.01, ME 2

items.check: Staff can check, at the point of care, what a physician working here is privileged to do.
items.howToCheck: Ask the nurse to show you how they would check.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a standardized, objective, evidence-based process to grant or deny privileges for medical staff members and others permitted to practice independently.
jciRefs.meText: The clinical privileges of all medical staff members are made available to those individuals or locations in the hospital in which the medical staff member will provide services.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — SQE.06.00, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a standardized, objective, evidence-based process to grant or deny privileges for medical staff members and others permitted to practice independently.
jciRefs.meText: Each medical staff member provides only those services that have been specifically granted by the hospital.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — SQE.06.00, ME 4

items.check: Staff can describe de-escalation, who to call for security, and how a workplace violence incident is reported — and the training is documented.
items.howToCheck: Ask: a relative becomes threatening at this station — walk me through it.
items.evidenceAskWho: Ask: Staff Nurse. Review training record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Leaders and staff are trained and demonstrate competence in workplace violence prevention.
jciRefs.meText: The training, education, and resources address prevention, recognition, response, and reporting of workplace violence as follows: • What constitutes workplace violence (See also GLD.07.02, ME 2) • Education on the roles and responsibilities of leaders, clinical staff, security personnel, and external law enforcement • Training in early detection, de-escalation, nonphysical intervention skills, physical intervention techniques, and response to emergency incidents • The reporting process for workplace violence incidents (See also GLD.07.02, ME 5)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — SQE.02.02, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: Leaders and staff are trained and demonstrate competence in workplace violence prevention.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital provides training, education, and resources (at time of hire, annually, and whenever changes occur regarding the workplace violence prevention program) to leaders, and staff. (See also GLD.07.02, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — SQE.02.02, ME 1

items.check: Triage uses the evidence-based process for this population, includes early recognition of communicable disease, and triage staff are trained in it.
items.howToCheck: Observe a triage decision. Ask the triage nurse about communicable disease recognition and check their training.
items.evidenceAskWho: Observe. Ask: Triage Nurse. Review training record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: Patients with emergent, urgent, or immediate needs are given priority for assessment and treatment.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital selects and uses an evidence-based triage process, appropriate to its patient population, to identify and prioritize patients with emergent, urgent, and immediate needs.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Patients with emergent, urgent, or immediate needs are given priority for assessment and treatment.
jciRefs.meText: The triage process includes early recognition of communicable diseases.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.01, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: Patients with emergent, urgent, or immediate needs are given priority for assessment and treatment.
jciRefs.meText: Staff are trained to use the triage process, including the early recognition of communicable diseases.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.01, ME 4

items.check: Boarded patients held in this area have the space, staffing, resources and care their condition requires.
items.howToCheck: Look at where boarded patients are held and ask how their care is maintained.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital has a process for managing the flow of patients throughout the hospital that includes the admission and registration of patients, as applicable to the patient care setting.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital plans and provides for the care of patients who are boarded in the emergency department and other temporary holding areas, including the following: • Allocation of space, utilities, equipment, medical equipment, and supplies • Staffing plans • Availability of clinical resources • Availability of nonclinical resources • Provision of timely and equivalent care to meet patient needs • A time limit on boarding patients in the emergency department and other temporary holding areas and a process for managing patients when temporary boarding periods exceed this time limit
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.02.00, ME 3

jciRefs.standardStatement: Patients with emergent, urgent, or immediate needs are given priority for assessment and treatment.
jciRefs.meText: There is a process for holding patients for observation when clinically indicated.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ACC.01.01, ME 5

items.check: Preprocedure verification is completed and documented, covering consent, correct patient/procedure/site, required equipment and implants present, blood loss risk, difficult airway or aspiration risk, and known allergies.
items.howToCheck: Take one case and check the completed checklist against every required element.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the preoperative verification and surgical/invasive procedure site marking.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital implements a preoperative verification process using a checklist or other mechanism to document verification of the following: • Informed consent that is appropriate to the procedure • Correct patient, correct procedure, and correct site • All required documents, blood products, medical equipment, and implantable medical devices are on hand, correct, and functional • Whether there is a risk of blood loss > 500 mL (7 mL/kg in children) • Whether the patient has a difficult airway or aspiration risk • Any known allergies (See also PCC.03.00, ME 2)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.00, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: Each patient’s surgical care is planned based on the results of the preoperative assessment and documented in the patient’s medical record.
jciRefs.meText: A preoperative diagnosis and the planned surgical procedure are documented in the patient’s medical record prior to the procedure.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — ASC.04.00, ME 4

items.check: The site is marked with the hospital's single unambiguous mark, by the person doing the procedure, with the patient involved — and there are written alternatives for refusal, potential harm and technically impossible marking.
items.howToCheck: Observe a marking. Ask the patient if they were involved. Ask to see the three written alternatives.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the preoperative verification and surgical/invasive procedure site marking.
jciRefs.meText: The hospital uses an instantly recognizable and unambiguous mark for identifying the surgical/ invasive site that is consistent throughout the hospital.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.00, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the preoperative verification and surgical/invasive procedure site marking.
jciRefs.meText: The surgical/invasive site marking process includes the following: • Marking completed by the person performing the procedure • Patient involved in the marking process • Alternative site-marking process for cases in which marking may result in harm • Alternative site-identification process for patients who refuse site marking • Alternative site-marking techniques for situations in which routine site marking is not possible (for example, laser, stereotactic radiosurgery, dental)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.00, ME 3

items.check: The full team actively participates in a documented time-out in the procedure area immediately before starting, and a repeat time-out is performed before each new procedure by a different surgeon.
items.howToCheck: Observe a time-out. Watch whether everyone actually stops and participates.

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the time-out that is performed immediately prior to the start of the surgical/invasive procedure and the sign-out that is conducted after the procedure.
jciRefs.meText: The full team actively participates in a time-out process, which includes the following elements in the area in which the surgical/invasive procedure will be performed, immediately before starting the procedure, and this is documented: • Correct patient identity • Correct procedure to be done • Correct surgical/invasive procedure site
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.01, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: The hospital implements a process for the time-out that is performed immediately prior to the start of the surgical/invasive procedure and the sign-out that is conducted after the procedure.
jciRefs.meText: When two or more separate procedures are being performed on the same patient by different surgeons, the team must perform another time-out before each new procedure is initiated.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — IPSG.04.01, ME 4

items.check: Where radiation or imaging is used in this area, staff are trained, protective equipment is available and worn, and dose optimisation practice is followed.
items.howToCheck: Observe use. Check lead protection and the training record.

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 1

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: Radiology and diagnostic imaging staff are oriented to safety requirements and receive ongoing education and training for any new procedures, equipment, and hazardous materials. (See also SQE.01.07, ME 1)
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 2

jciRefs.standardStatement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is implemented and is compliant with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
jciRefs.meText: Safety protective equipment and devices appropriate to the practices and hazards encountered from radiation and diagnostic imaging are available to staff, patients, and visitors, and in the area in which radiology and diagnostic imaging services are provided.
jciRefs.exactSource: JCI Hospital Standards for Hospitals, 8th Edition — AOP.05.02, ME 3
